correctness.rationale: The unconditioned discrete-time Moran absorption problem has transient states the nonempty proper mutant subsets S, birth-death transition probabilities 1/(n deg(u)) for each oriented disagreeing edge, and self-loops for unchanged attempts. First-step conditioning gives (I-Q)a=1, (I-Q)b=2a-1; mixture over all singleton starts gives mean (1/n)sum a_singleton and variance (1/n)sum b_singleton minus the squared mixture mean. Independent exact rational linear algebra reimplemented from the model, rather than from saved outputs, exhaustively tested the 0, 3, 84 and 3140 labeled connected-graph/nonedge cases for orders 2,3,4,5 (zero discordant signs). Both six-vertex displayed edge-insertion witnesses were recomputed exactly, including the full four huge rational differences, and have opposite strict mean/variance signs in both possible directions. Exhaustion proves only <=5 lower bound; n=6 examples prove upper bound, not six-vertex uniqueness.

value.rationale: Mean absorption duration and its variance quantify genuinely different stability/risk dimensions in evolutionary stochastic networks. A single-edge intervention can improve expectation while worsening fluctuation or vice versa, first possible at a sharp graph order, making the finite cutoff and both directions a meaningful complete qualitative boundary. This is not merely a known mean phenomenon reworded.
